To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

a new antenna concept is introduced and successfully demonstrated to more than halve the size of conventional LP antennas for dual-circular polarized (DCP) operation while maintaining the same bandwidth.
we designed a 2.3 smaller dual-polarized log-periodic antenna that works from 500 to 3 GHz and is high-power capable.
a novel 4-arm log periodic antenna design that has a 2.3x smaller size than conventional log periodic antennas is demonstrated and its high-power capabilities are verified.
In summary, our research is concerned with
developing a compact dual-polarized LP antenna for use as a high-power transmit and receive antenna.
the design, fabrication, and testing of a reduced size planar log-periodic dual-circularly-polarized antenna for high power transmit/receive (TX/RX) applications.
the development of a new type of high-power bidirectional dual-circularly-polarized antenna.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the antenna is a reduced size dual-polarized bidirectional antenna that is high-power capable and has a very broad bandwidth.
a high-power dual-polarized antenna with a reduced size is demonstrated and its performance characterized for a variety of applications.
this work has successfully demonstrated the feasibility of a compact dual-polarized antenna that is high-power capable and can be used for bidirectional high power transmission/reception.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
a dual-polarized bidirectional LP with a bandwidth of 1:6 and a turn-on frequency of 500 MHz has been designed, prototyped, and tested to work with 100 W CW power.
a 4-arm LP antenna can be made smaller by 2.3x by manipulating the ground plane currents to form a ring aperture and that this antenna is high power stable.
the antenna can be used in a variety of high-power bidirectional applications such as radar, communication, and radio-frequency identification.
The main takeaway from our work is that
by manipulating the ground plane currents of an LP, the overall antenna bandwidth can be increased.
by using a simple ground plane manipulation technique, a 2.3× reduction in size can be achieved with only a 0.3 GHz reduction in bandwidth.
a high power bidirectional dual-CP LP antenna can be made 2.3 smaller than its conventional counterpart.
